Why don't birds get fried on power lines? 🐦⚡

Current only flows when there's a voltage difference. A bird's two feet grip the same wire at almost the same voltage, so almost nothing flows through it. Touch two wires at once, though...

#physics #electricity #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why are airplane windows round? ✈️

Early jets had square windows — and the sharp corners concentrated stress until they cracked in flight. Rounded corners spread the stress out. Engineers learned this the hard way with the de Havilland Comet.

#engineering #aviation #planes #learnontiktok #edutainment

Your phone's GPS needs Einstein. 🛰️

Clocks on GPS satellites tick faster than clocks on the ground — gravity and speed combined add about 38 microseconds a day. Ignore relativity and your location drifts roughly 10 km every day.

#physics #space #gps #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

The Sahara used to be green — with lakes, grass, and hippos. 🌿

About 6,000 years ago a slow wobble in Earth's orbit pulled the monsoon rains north and the desert bloomed. The wobble will swing back... in a few thousand years.

#geography #earth #sahara #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Steel sinks — so how do steel ships float? 🚢

A ship is mostly air. Its hull pushes aside more water-weight than the whole ship weighs, so it floats. Archimedes figured this out over 2,000 years ago.

#physics #science #ships #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why did this bridge start dancing? 🌉

When London's Millennium Bridge opened, the crowd's footsteps synced with its tiny sway and amplified it into a wobble. They closed it after two days. It's called synchronous lateral excitation.

#engineering #physics #bridges #learnontiktok #edutainment

You see lightning, then hear thunder seconds later. Why? ⚡

Light is basically instant; sound only travels ~343 m/s. Count the seconds from flash to bang and divide by 3 — that's how many kilometres away the strike is.

#physics #weather #lightning #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Spaceships don't burn up from friction. 🚀

At ~7.8 km/s a returning capsule slams into the air faster than it can move aside, compressing it into a shock layer thousands of degrees hot. The heat comes from squeezing the air, not rubbing it.

#space #physics #reentry #spacecraft #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

There's a 660-tonne ball hanging inside this skyscraper. 🏢

It's a tuned mass damper. The wind sways the tower; the giant sphere swings the opposite way, tuned to the building's own rhythm, and cancels the wobble.

#engineering #architecture #skyscraper #physics #learnontiktok #edutainment

Ice should sink — but it floats. ❄️

Water expands when it freezes into an open lattice, so ice is only ~92% as dense as water (just the tip of the iceberg shows). That floating cap insulates lakes so fish survive winter.

#chemistry #physics #water #ice #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

The loneliest place on Earth — where the nearest people are in space. 🛰️

At Point Nemo the closest land is ~2,688 km away. But the ISS orbits just ~400 km up, so when it passes over, the nearest humans are the astronauts overhead. It's also the 'spacecraft cemetery.'

#geography #ocean #space #iss #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why does the Moon always show us the same face? 🌕

It's tidally locked — it spins exactly once for every lap around Earth (~27.3 days), so one side stays pointed at us. And the 'dark side' isn't dark; it gets the same sunlight. It's just the far side.

#space #astronomy #moon #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

You can't fold paper to the Moon — but the math says 42. 📄

Each fold doubles the thickness. 0.1 mm doubled 42 times shoots past the Moon. In real life you jam up around 7 folds: the stack becomes thicker than it is wide. That's exponential growth.

#math #science #exponential #paper #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why is the sky blue? 🌤️

Sunlight is every colour mixed. Air scatters short blue waves far more than red (by one over wavelength to the fourth), so blue fills the sky from every direction. At sunset the light crosses more air, the blue scatters away, and you're left with red.

#physics #optics #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Do sinks drain backwards in Australia? 🌀

That's a myth — the Coriolis effect is far too weak to steer a sink; the drain's shape wins. But over something huge like a hurricane it's decisive: storms spin counter-clockwise up north, clockwise down south, and can't even form right at the equator where it drops to zero.

#physics #geography #weather #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

How do noise-cancelling headphones erase sound? 🎧

Not thick foam. A tiny mic samples the incoming noise, and the speaker plays that exact wave flipped upside down. Crest meets trough and they add to nothing — destructive interference.

#physics #sound #waves #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why are golf balls covered in dimples? ⛳

They're aerodynamic. A smooth ball drags a wide wake; dimples trip the air into a thin turbulent layer that clings on, shrinking the wake and roughly halving the drag. It's called the drag crisis — and it makes the ball fly about twice as far.

#physics #aerodynamics #golf #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why doesn't the Leaning Tower of Pisa fall over? 🗼

No glue — just balance. A tower tips only when its centre of mass passes outside its base. Pisa's weight sits only about 2 metres off-centre, and its base is nearly 8 metres wide. It could lean to about 15 degrees before it would ever topple.

#physics #engineering #architecture #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why do we add a leap day? 📅

It's not for February — it's Earth's orbit. A year is about 365.2422 days, not a round number, so that spare quarter-day piles up. We add a day every four years, then skip three leaps every 400 years. That's why 2000 counted but 1900 didn't, and it keeps the calendar within a day of the seasons for millennia.

#astronomy #calendar #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Mountaintops are closer to the Sun, so why are they freezing? 🏔️

Because a few kilometres is nothing next to 150 million km to the Sun. The real reason is pressure: air thins and expands as it rises, and expanding air cools — about 6.5 °C for every kilometre you climb.

#physics #weather #atmosphere #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Astronauts float because there's no gravity in space... right? 🚀

Wrong - gravity up there is still about 90% as strong as down here. They float because they're falling the whole time, while moving sideways at nearly 8 km every second. The ground curves away as fast as they fall, so they keep missing the Earth. That endless fall is an orbit.

#space #physics #astronauts #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why does metal feel colder than wood? 🥶

It isn't colder - both are at room temperature. Your skin doesn't feel temperature, it feels heat leaving. Metal pulls heat out of your hand fast, so your skin drops to about 21 °C. Wood barely takes any, so it stays near 30 °C. Same reason tiles feel colder than a rug.

#physics #heat #science #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why can't you ever reach the end of a rainbow? 🌈

Because it isn't a thing in a place. Sunlight enters each raindrop, bounces off the back and comes out bent at about 42 degrees. The rainbow is every drop sitting at that angle from your eye - move and it moves with you. It's really a full circle; the ground just hides the bottom half.

#physics #optics #light #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

If you can see into a microwave, why can't the microwaves get out? 🍿

The glass hides a metal mesh with holes about a millimetre wide. A microwave is a wave 12 cm long - far too big to squeeze through, so it bounces back. Light waves are thousands of times smaller than the holes, so they sail right out. You get the view, the popcorn gets the heat.

#physics #waves #technology #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Why do stars twinkle but planets don't? ✨

The star isn't flickering - our air is. Moving pockets of warm and cold air bend the light back and forth in its last split second. A star is a single point, so the whole thing wobbles. A planet is a tiny disc, so its wobbles average out. From space, stars don't twinkle at all.

#astronomy #space #stars #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

Rivers are fresh, so why is the sea salty? 🌊

The salt comes from the rivers. Rain slowly dissolves rock, and rivers carry a tiny pinch of those minerals to the sea. Then the Sun evaporates the water, but the salt stays behind. Repeat for a few billion years and every litre of seawater holds about 35 grams of salt.

#earthscience #ocean #geography #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts

One Moon... so why two high tides a day? 🌕

The Moon pulls hardest on the near side of the Earth and weakest on the far side. That difference stretches the ocean into two bulges - one facing the Moon, one facing away. The Earth spins under both, so high tide comes about every 12 and a half hours.

#physics #ocean #moon #learnontiktok #edutainment #sciencefacts
